schema.title: O*NET occupation title (O*NET 31.0 Occupation Data)
schema.riasec: [R,I,A,S,E,C] O*NET Occupational Interest ratings, 1-7 (O*NET 31.0 Career Interest Types, scale OI). Every occupation here carries them; career_match.py still accepts null for a code-only occupation
schema.high_point_code: O*NET's own First/Second/Third Interest High-Point as 1-3 Holland letters (O*NET 31.0, scale IH)
schema.job_zone: O*NET Job Zone, integer 1-5 (O*NET 31.0 Job Zones)
schema.source_url: O*NET OnLine page where the occupation was first observed (a Browse-by-Interests list or the occupation's summary page); the numbers come from the database files in fetched_from
schema.work_values: {value_name: rank 1-6} ipsative ranking (1=most important) over the six O*NET Work Values, or null when O*NET 30.2 does not rate the occupation
schema.work_values_extent_1_7: the six 1-7 Extent scores the ranking was derived from (O*NET 30.2 Work Values, scale EX), or null
schema.work_values_db: O*NET Database release the Work Values came from ("30.2"), or null

notes.build: Built by tools/build_occupations.py from the O*NET 31.0 text database (Occupation Data.txt, Career Interest Types.txt, Job Zones.txt) and, for Work Values, the O*NET 30.2 text database (Work Values.txt), for the SOC codes this file already listed. A value O*NET does not publish is null; nothing is estimated.
notes.interest_source: O*NET marks the Domain Source of these interest ratings as Machine Learning/Expert for 1116 and Machine Learning for 12 of the 1128 ratings here: they are O*NET's model estimates, and should be described that way.
notes.work_values_ranks: work_values ranks the six Extent scores from highest to lowest and breaks ties alphabetically by value name, the order of career_match.WORK_VALUES.
notes.mapped_terms: Terms with no dedicated O*NET-SOC code were mapped to the nearest real code and disclosed, not fabricated: 'medical physicist'/'MRI physicist' -> Physicists 19-2012.00; 'machine learning / AI engineer' -> Data Scientists 15-2051.00 and Computer and Information Research Scientists 15-1221.00.
notes.not_rated_for_work_values: 15 occupations have no Work Values in O*NET 30.2 and carry work_values: null: Data Scientists 15-2051.00; Software Developers 15-1252.00; Penetration Testers 15-1299.04; Digital Forensics Analysts 15-1299.06; Medical Dosimetrists 29-2036.00; Web and Digital Interface Designers 15-1255.00; Cardiologists 29-1212.00; Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars 29-9021.00; Medical Records Specialists 29-2072.00; Blockchain Engineers 15-1299.07; Financial and Investment Analysts 13-2051.00; Emergency Medical Technicians 29-2042.00; Paramedics 29-2043.00; Project Management Specialists 13-1082.00; Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel 41-3091.00.

scale_note: riasec holds O*NET Occupational Interests (elements 1.B.1.a-f, scale OI), 1-7, higher = stronger interest, from the O*NET 31.0 Database (Career Interest Types.txt). high_point_code is O*NET's First/Second/Third Interest High-Point (elements 1.B.1.g/h/i, scale IH), mapped 1=R, 2=I, 3=A, 4=S, 5=E, 6=C, with 0 meaning no further high point. In every occupation here the first high point is one of the highest of the six ratings. work_values_extent_1_7 holds the six O*NET Work Values (elements 1.B.2.a-f, scale EX, Extent), 1-7, from the O*NET 30.2 Database.
coverage_note: 188 occupations across all six RIASEC areas, still weighted toward the author's own field (data science, ML, research, computing, medical imaging) with a spread across healthcare, skilled trades, arts, social services and education, business, sales and law, and administration and finance. All 188 carry numeric interest ratings; 173 also carry Work Values. Common occupations such as Preschool Teachers, Except Special Education; Police and Sheriff's Patrol Officers; Couriers and Messengers; and Light Truck Drivers are in O*NET 31.0 but not in this file.
work_values_discontinuation_note: O*NET no longer publishes Work Values: the O*NET 31.0 text database has no Work Values.txt, so Work Values here come from 30.2, an older release than the interest data. Occupations 30.2 does not rate carry work_values: null, not an estimate.
